Built-in SEO for documentation sites — sitemap, robots, llms.txt, per-page meta tags, and crawlable static HTML.

Top-level seo block in aiui.yaml: Every key is optional; the defaults are what most sites want. siteUrl is needed for absolute canonical URLs and sitemap.xml. Without it the build falls back to a CNAME file next to the config (or in docs/), and without either there is no sitemap and llms.txt / llms-full.txt use root-relative links. What the build publishes for agents (agent-ready .md pages, llms.txt by nav group, markdown.instructions): AI-ready docs.

aiui build automatically generates: File Purpose sitemap.xml All doc URLs with lastmod dates robots.txt Crawl rules + sitemap pointer llms.txt AI crawler index (llmstxt.org), one section per nav group llms-full.txt Every page as agent-ready Markdown, in one file docs/**/*.html Per-route HTML with meta tags + crawl nav .nojekyll GitHub Pages Jekyll bypass No extra flags are needed: the files are written whenever content.docs is configured (the site-URL ones only when a site URL is known, see above). A robots.txt or sitemap.xml next to aiui.yaml is published as it is, instead of the generated one.

One rule decides the sitemap, llms.txt, llms-full.txt, site search and the page's robots meta, so they never disagree: Page Sidebar Sitemap, llms, search normal yes yes index, follow noindex: true yes no noindex hidden no no (yes with seo.indexing: all) noindex (index, follow with all) any, with seo.robots.index: false as above no sitemap or llms files; search kept noindex searchable: false yes sitemap and llms yes; site search no index, follow Each page has exactly one robots meta tag. noindex does not add nofollow: crawlers still follow the page's links to the pages that are indexed. With seo.robots.index: false, robots.txt says Disallow: /, and no sitemap.xml or llms*.txt is written (one left from an earlier build is removed).

A hidden page is built and reachable by its URL (share the link), but it is not in the sidebar, the previous / next links or search, and not indexed. In content.docs.nav.mode: manual, hidden: true on a group or tab hides all its pages, and pages no group lists are hidden too (Navigation). A folder without an index.md is a sidebar section only, never a page: it gets no route and no sitemap entry.

seo.contentSignals writes a Content-Signal line into robots.txt, saying how crawlers may use the pages: search (search results), aiInput (answers grounded on the page) and aiTrain (model training). Keys you leave out are left out of the line; with no contentSignals there is no line.

Use frontmatter on any markdown page: If description is omitted, the first paragraph is used automatically. Component and HTML tags are left out of it: a page that opens with or a multi-line gets its first sentence of prose. Any Open Graph, Twitter or article tag, the canonical URL, the robots value and keywords can be set per page (quote keys that have a colon): Each tag is decided once, in this order (later wins): the built defaults, seo.metatags, seo.paths (shorter paths first), the page's frontmatter. Then og:url follows the canonical and twitter:image the og:image (unless set themselves), and twitter:card is summary_large_image when the page has an image. Root-relative URLs (/images/x.png) become absolute. A noindex page keeps noindex whatever the overrides say, and a robots value with noindex (from frontmatter or a seo.paths folder) also leaves the page out of the sitemap, llms.txt and search, so they never disagree. Open Graph keys (og:, article:) are written as property=, the rest as name=; every value is HTML-escaped. aiui validate rejects a seo.metatags key that is not a tag name.

Install Pillow and every docs page gets its own share image, with no config: The build draws a 1200x630 PNG per page and publishes it at /og/ .png (/og/docs/guide/install.png). Each card shows the page title (sized to fit, up to three lines), its sidebar group, as much of the description as fits, the site name with its logo and the site's host, in the theme's accent and colour mode (site.theme.preset, accent, accentDark, mode; preset paper gets the paper colours). A PNG, JPEG, WebP or GIF logo is drawn as is; an SVG or emoji logo becomes the site's initial on an accent tile. Latin text uses the UI's own font; other scripts use a system font (Noto Sans CJK, Arial Unicode, Noto Sans or DejaVu Sans). The card becomes the page's og:image and twitter:image, with a summary_large_image card, in the built HTML and when the docs app moves between pages, and the site root shares the docs home's card. Which image a page gets, first match wins: Set by Image 'og:image' in the page's frontmatter or a seo.paths folder that image, no card drawn og:image in seo.metatags that image on every page, no cards drawn seo.ogImages: false, or Pillow not installed seo.defaultImage otherwise the page's generated card Cards are cached by a hash of what they show (in $AIUI_DATA_DIR/og-cards, else ~/.praisonaiui/cache/og-cards), so aiui dev and repeat builds only draw the pages that changed, and new cards are drawn in parallel. Without Pillow, aiui build prints one note saying how to turn them on.

Each route HTML file contains: (absolute HTTPS) Open Graph tags (og:title, og:description, og:url, og:type, og:site_name, og:image: the page's social card by default), each once Twitter Card tags (summary_large_image with an image) Your seo.metatags, seo.paths and frontmatter tags One JSON-LD @graph: Organization, WebSite (with a SearchAction: ?q= opens site search), TechArticle (publisher, dateModified with content.docs.lastUpdated, keywords, image) and a BreadcrumbList from the sidebar groups Static with links to every doc page (for non-JS crawlers) pre-rendered page content

When users navigate via the sidebar, React updates title, canonical, OG, Twitter, robots, and JSON-LD to match the current page, with the same tags, overrides and order as the built HTML (docs-nav.json carries each page's seo map). The built page's JSON-LD graph stays while it is the page shown.
